title: そのために — for that purpose / because of that
summary: A conjunction that begins a sentence and points back to the previous sentence. It can mean “for that purpose” (a goal) or “because of that” (a cause). Most often it is the purpose use, as in 医者になりたい。そのために、〜.

body.p: The previous sentence is a goal or plan, and the next sentence is the action taken to realize it. In 来年留学します。そのために、お金を貯めています, the two connect directly. The second sentence usually has a deliberate action such as 貯めている or 勉強している.

As in 台風が来た。そのために、電車が止まった, it can also say that something happened as a result of that. Whether it is purpose or cause is decided by the second sentence: a deliberate action means purpose, a naturally occurring event means cause. To state cause clearly you can also say そのせいで or そのため.

examples.ja: 来年（らいねん）留学（りゅうがく）します。そのために、お金（かね）を貯（た）めています。
examples.romaji: Rainen ryūgaku shimasu. Sono tame ni, okane o tamete imasu.
examples.tr: I'll study abroad next year. For that, I'm saving money.
examples.note: Purpose: saving money to study abroad.

examples.ja: 医者（いしゃ）になりたい。そのために、毎日（まいにち）遅（おそ）くまで勉強（べんきょう）している。
examples.romaji: Isha ni naritai. Sono tame ni, mainichi osoku made benkyō shite iru.
examples.tr: I want to become a doctor. For that reason, I study late every day.

examples.ja: 来月（らいげつ）、家族（かぞく）で旅行（りょこう）する。そのために、少（すこ）しずつ準備（じゅんび）を始（はじ）めた。
examples.romaji: Raigetsu, kazoku de ryokō suru. Sono tame ni, sukoshi zutsu junbi o hajimeta.
examples.tr: Next month we'll travel as a family. For that, I've started preparing little by little.

pitfalls: The previous sentence must be a goal or event; その points back to the whole sentence.
For cause, make the next sentence a natural event; for purpose, make it a deliberate action.
